svg.title: Physical model of the lung collapse
svg.desc: Left: in vivo the inflated lung fills the chest cavity, held open by the pleural pressure, which is lower at the top; its gradient carries the weight of the lung. Right: in the pneumothorax that pressure is lost; the load is an inward pressure, uniform part plus gradient, the lung shrinks towards the clamped hilum and rests on the dependent chest wall. Below: patient positions and the direction of gravity in the reference CT and during the collapse; the limit of compression (tissue and air trapped by emphysema, an optional barrier), and the table of the parameters.
svg.text: pleural under-pressure, larger at the top:
its gradient ρ̄g ≈ 2 Pa/mm carries the weight (Archimedes):
−∮ ppl​ n dA = ρ̄ g V eh​, eh​ = −eA​
load = the pleural pressure that is lost, on the free surface:
chest wall (dashed): margin A, rigid, frictionless;
solid brown: contact, the wall now carries the weight
Non-dimensional load (only ratios to E matter for the shape)
q(X) = Δp / E = q0​ + γ (h(X) − h̄), q0​ = p0​ / E, γ = ρ̄ g / E, h = −eA​ · X
Patient position: gravity eA​ in the inflated CT, eB​ during the collapse (LPS axes)
Limit of compression (optional barrier): the lung cannot lose more than the air that can leave
φ = ρ̄CT​ / ρt​ + ε r fe​
tissue: ρ̄CT​ from the CT (mass / volume), ρt​ = 1050 kg/m³
trapped air: ε = emphysema yes / no (user), fe​ = LAA%−950
of the CT, r = 0.54 of it does not leave (cohort)
W = WNH​ + κE ⟨Jon​ − J⟩³₊ / (J − φ), Jon​ = φ + 0.1
zero above Jon​: the calibrated collapses are unchanged;
a surgical pressure (12 mmHg) stops the lung just above φ
Parameters: each one given (a number) or fitted to the collapsed CT
uniform pressure released: sets the collapse %
effective stiffness of the lung tissue
mean density of the inflated lung (model)
the same measured on the CT
emphysema: yes / no (user); its volume (CT LAA%)
chest wall: margin, smoothing of the field
E rule (13 fitted patients, ν 0.30, ρ̄ 200 kg/m³): log10​ E [Pa] = 3.54 − 0.0129 × collapse % → ≈ 1.6 kPa at 25 %, 0.78 kPa at 50 %
